claims.text: The proposed intervention uses alloy electrodes fabricated by spark plasma sintering, followed by multilayer electrospark deposition on damaged steel surfaces.
The target steel components have microstructural heterogeneities that predispose them to hot cracking.
The proposed process will produce a dense coating.
The proposed process will produce a well-adhered, metallurgically bonded coating.
The deposited multilayer coating will have a graded microstructure transitioning from the deposited material to the steel substrate.
Controlled electrospark-deposition energy input will minimize thermal input.
Minimizing thermal input will limit additional substrate microstructural damage.
Spark plasma sintering produces fine, homogeneous alloyed powders.
Layer-by-layer electrospark deposition using the sintered electrodes creates a refined-grain coating.
A refined coating and graded interface improve mechanical integrity.
The refined and graded interface reduces crack initiation under thermal stress.
The deposited alloy composition enhances surface hardness.
The deposited alloy composition enhances corrosion resistance.
The proposed coating will have higher hardness than both fusion-welded repairs and untreated damaged surfaces.
The proposed coating will have better wear resistance than both fusion-welded repairs and untreated damaged surfaces.
The proposed coating will have better corrosion resistance than both fusion-welded repairs and untreated damaged surfaces.
The proposed coating will show less hot-crack or surface-crack initiation under thermal cycling than both fusion-welded repairs and untreated damaged surfaces.
The improved surface properties will extend service life in corrosive, elevated-temperature, and cyclic-wear environments.
The intervention is applicable to in-situ surface repair of high-value steel components when substrate temperature can be controlled.
The intervention may not apply to non-ferrous alloys or repairs requiring restoration of bulk properties.

contradictions.description: The intervention describes spark plasma sintering as converting alloy powders into electrodes, whereas the mechanism says spark plasma sintering produces fine, homogeneous alloyed powders. These statements assign inconsistent products to the same processing step.
